title: Keep every sentence, however short
statement: A check that matches answers to the text must keep every sentence that carries a content word, however short.
example: A minimum of 10 characters dropped a one-word sentence of exactly 10 and made a correctly keyed answer look unsupported.
detail: A content audit for Grade 3 reading lessons splits each story into sentences to check that a keyed answer is supported by the text. An earlier minimum length of 10 characters silently dropped one-word sentences, which is where that prose puts its key words, and made a correctly keyed answer look unsupported; the splitter now keeps every sentence that carries a content word (`shadow/content-eval/SKILL.md`).

evidence.quote: Sentence splitting keeps **every** sentence carrying a content word.

An earlier minimum length of 10 characters silently dropped one-word dramatic sentences — `"Gratitude."` is exactly 10 — which is where this prose puts its key words, and it made a correctly-keyed answer look unsupported.
